module.purpose: Provides reactive effect scheduling primitives that track signal dependencies, respond to state epochs, and support immediate or deferred execution.
module.summary: This module implements dependency-aware side-effect scheduling for the state library. It maintains parent signals, epochs, attachment state, and scheduling counts; captures dependencies while effects execute; avoids rerunning effects when relevant parents are unchanged; and supports optional external scheduling callbacks. It exposes a scheduler constructor plus convenience APIs for one-shot lifecycle management and restartable reactors.
module.businessContext: Supports reactive UI and application state integrations by running effects when observed state changes. Failures can leave derived views, DOM effects, or framework integrations stale or incorrectly scheduled.

preconditions: The scheduler instance has initialized _isActivelyListening, lastReactedEpoch, and parents state.
Global epoch and parent-change tracking are available.
postconditions: If the scheduler is inactive, no scheduling occurs.
If the current global epoch equals lastReactedEpoch, no scheduling occurs.
If relevant parents have not changed after a prior reaction or parent capture, lastReactedEpoch is updated to the current global epoch and no scheduling occurs.
If execution is required, scheduleEffect() is invoked.
invariants: An inactive scheduler is never scheduled by this method.
An effect is not scheduled more than once for the same global epoch.
An effect that has never run is scheduled even when it has no captured parents.

edgeCases: When _isActivelyListening is false, the method returns immediately without reading further scheduling conditions.
When lastReactedEpoch equals the current global epoch, the method returns without scheduling.
When the effect has previously reacted or has captured at least one parent and no parent changed, lastReactedEpoch is advanced to the current global epoch and scheduling is skipped.
When the effect has never reacted and has captured no parents, the method schedules the effect.
When a relevant parent changed since the last reaction, the method schedules the effect.

/**
 * The reactor is a user-friendly interface for starting and stopping an `EffectScheduler`.
 *
 * Calling `.start()` will attach the scheduler and execute the effect immediately the first time it is called.
 *
 * If the reactor is stopped, calling `.start()` will re-attach the scheduler but will only execute the effect if any of its parents have changed since it was stopped.
 *
 * You can create a reactor with {@link reactor}.

detail.name: react
detail.summary: Provides the module's react entry point for coordinating effect scheduling and cleanup.

units.name: reactor

detail.name: reactor
postconditions: Starting invokes scheduler.attach() before scheduling logic.
When force is true, starting invokes scheduler.scheduleEffect().
When force is false, starting invokes scheduler.maybeScheduleEffect().
invariants: The scheduling path is selected by the force option at start time.
Stopping delegates scheduler lifecycle cleanup to scheduler.detach().
edgeCases: With force=true, start uses unconditional scheduling via scheduleEffect().
With force=false, start uses conditional scheduling via maybeScheduleEffect().
Calling stop delegates to detach without performing scheduling.
stateMutations: Scheduler attachment, scheduling, and detachment state through the scheduler instance.
detail.summary: Creates reactor lifecycle controls that attach the scheduler on start and detach it on stop. Starting either force-schedules the effect or conditionally schedules it through the scheduler.
